examples.en: The mayor attended the completion ceremony of the new library.

examples.ko: 다리 준공식이 다음 주 토요일에 열려요.
examples.en: The bridge's completion ceremony will be held next Saturday.

examples.ko: 준공식 날에는 주민들이 모여 함께 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the day of the completion ceremony, residents gathered and took photos together.

examples.ko: 아버지 회사가 지은 건물의 준공식에 초대받았어요.
examples.en: I was invited to the completion ceremony of a building my father's company built.
With the completion ceremony coming up, the final cleaning is in full swing.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 준공식은 실내에서 간단히 진행됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the completion ceremony was held simply indoors.

explain: 건물, 도로, 다리 같은 공사가 끝났을 때 하는 행사예요. 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사는 '착공식'이라고 하고, 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The bridge groundbreaking ceremony was held last spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사로, 준공식과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony held when construction begins; good to remember as a pair with 준공식.

phrases.example: 시청은 다음 달에 새 건물 준공식을 열 거예요.
phrases.en: City Hall will hold a completion ceremony for the new building next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 연다고 할 때 '열다'를 붙이는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 열다 for holding the event.

phrases.en: We invited the mayor to the completion ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 행사에 부를 때 '-에 초대하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-에 초대하다' when inviting someone to the event.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to the completion ceremony

explain_en: It is the ceremony held when construction of a building, road or bridge is finished. The ceremony held when construction starts is '착공식', so it helps to remember the two as a pair.

examples.en: The hospital decided to increase its nursing staff.

examples.ko: 회사가 연말까지 직원을 열 명 증원해요.
examples.en: The company is adding ten employees by the end of the year.

examples.ko: 경찰은 축제 기간에 순찰 인력을 증원했어요.
examples.en: The police increased patrol personnel during the festival.

examples.ko: 인원을 증원하면 일이 훨씬 수월해질 거예요.
examples.en: If we add more staff, the work will get much easier.

examples.ko: 대학이 입학 정원을 증원한다는 소식이 나왔어요.
examples.en: News came out that the university will increase its admission quota.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 증원하자는 의견이 회의에서 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people in the meeting suggested adding people to our team.

explain: 사람 수, 곧 인원이나 병력, 정원을 늘릴 때만 써요. 물건이나 양이 늘 때는 쓰지 않아요. 반대말은 '감원'이고, 일상에서는 '사람을 더 뽑다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: We increase the number of part-time staff in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인원, 인력, 병력'처럼 사람 수를 나타내는 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with words for people counts like headcount or personnel.

phrases.example: 일이 많아서 사람을 더 뽑기로 했어요.
phrases.en: There is a lot of work, so we decided to hire more people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '증원하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say the same thing.

phrases.en: The emergency room needs more doctors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '증원'으로 필요성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '증원' to talk about the need for more staff.

explain_en: It is used only for increasing the number of people, such as staff, troops, or quotas, not for objects or amounts. Its opposite is '감원' (staff reduction), and in daily talk people also say '사람을 더 뽑다'.

examples.ko: 인력 충원이 급해서 채용 공고를 냈어요.
examples.en: We urgently need more staff, so we posted a job notice.
We asked for more staff, but I heard the budget is short.

examples.ko: 이번 충원에서 열 명을 뽑을 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to take on ten people in this round of staffing.
We have to redo the staffing plan first.

examples.ko: 직원 충원 없이 일하려니 너무 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working without any added staff is really hard.
A vacancy opened up, so we started the process of filling it.

explain: '채용'은 사람을 새로 뽑는 일이고, '충원'은 부족하거나 빈 자리를 채운다는 점이 달라요. 회사, 학교, 팀 이야기에서 '인력 충원', '결원 충원'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The vacancies will be filled next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠진 자리를 채운다는 뜻이 잘 드러나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that clearly shows the idea of filling empty posts.

phrases.en: The team leader requested more staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 부족할 때 회사에 말하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking the company for more people due to a shortage.

phrases.en: Next year's hiring plan came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인원을 채울 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a plan to fill staff positions.

explain_en: '채용' is hiring people anew, while '충원' stresses filling a shortage or an empty spot. It is used in talk about companies, schools and teams, as in '인력 충원' and '결원 충원'.

en: to notify; to inform; to advise

examples.en: The school notifies parents of the results.
The company gave advance notice of the dismissal.
We will notify you of the changes by text message.

examples.ko: 통지하는 시기가 너무 늦어서 준비할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The notice came too late for me to prepare.
They are notifying people of results by email.
The court notified us of the date, so I found out.

explain: 공식적으로 어떤 사실을 알려 줄 때 써요. 친구에게 알려 줄 때는 '알려 주다'가 자연스럽고, '통지하다'는 회사·학교·관공서 같은 곳이 정해진 방법으로 알릴 때 써요. 같은 말의 명사는 '통지', 서류는 '통지서'예요.

phrases.en: I received notice of my acceptance yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 알림을 받았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you receive an official notice.

phrases.en: A notice arrived from the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 알리는 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document that gives official notice.

phrases.en: We will let you know the result by text message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy word used in everyday speech.

explain_en: It is for formally informing someone of a fact. To tell a friend, 알려 주다 is natural; 통지하다 is for institutions such as companies, schools, and offices notifying through set channels. The noun is 통지 and the document is 통지서.

en: to be sent; to be dispatched

examples.ko: 저는 다음 달에 일본 지사로 파견돼요.
examples.en: I'm being sent to the Japan branch next month.
Doctors were dispatched to the disaster area.

examples.ko: 파견된 직원들은 일 년 동안 현지에서 일해요.
examples.en: The dispatched staff work on site for a year.
More teachers are being sent to other schools.

examples.ko: 기자가 현장에 파견되면 바로 뉴스를 보낼 거예요.
examples.en: Once the reporter is sent to the scene, he will file news right away.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 두 명이 해외로 파견될 예정이에요.
examples.en: Two people from our team are scheduled to be sent overseas.

explain: 회사나 기관이 사람을 어떤 일을 하라고 다른 곳으로 보낼 때, 보내진 사람 입장에서 해요. '가다'와 달리 임무를 맡아 간다는 느낌이 있어요. 짧은 출장은 '출장 가다'라고 하고, 파견은 보통 더 길어요.

phrases.en: He was sent to an overseas branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디로 보내졌는지 '~로'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'to ~' to say where someone was sent.

phrases.en: I'm currently working on a dispatch assignment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 곳에 보내져 일하는 것을 가리키는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for working at a place you were sent to.

phrases.en: I'm going on assignment to Busan next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 자주 쓰는 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual expression often used in speech.

explain_en: From the viewpoint of the person sent: an organization sends someone to another place to do a job. Unlike the plain 가다, it implies going on an assigned duty. A short business trip is 출장, and 파견 is usually longer.

examples.en: You have to bring writing tools to the exam room.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 필기구가 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Writing tools are piled up on the desk.
I carry my writing tools in a separate part of my bag.
I bought new writing tools at the stationery store.
I had no pen, so I borrowed one from a friend.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 필기구가 종류별로 잘 정리되어 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has its writing supplies well organized by type.

explain: 펜, 연필처럼 글씨를 쓰는 도구를 한꺼번에 부를 때 써요. 말할 때는 '필기도구'를 더 많이 해요. 안내문이나 상품 분류에서 자주 봐요. 볼펜처럼 하나하나 말할 때는 이 말을 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I didn't bring my writing tools, so I borrowed some.
phrases.nuance_ko: '필기구'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 필기구, but more common in speech.

phrases.en: I packed my writing instruments before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 물건을 미리 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting needed items ready in advance.

phrases.en: I chose a pen at the writing instruments section of the stationery shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품을 나눠 놓은 곳에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen as a product category in stores.

explain_en: It is a group word for pens, pencils, and other writing tools. In speech, '필기도구' is more common. It shows up in notices and product categories. You would not use it for a single item like a ballpoint pen.

en: to put on the market; to release

examples.ko: 그 가수는 다음 주에 새 앨범을 발매해요.
examples.en: That singer is releasing a new album next week.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 게임을 올해 안에 발매하려고 해요.
examples.en: The company wants to release a new game within this year.
The song released last year is still popular.
Fans eagerly counted the days until it was released.
They released the limited edition first.
I hope they release the regular edition next year too.

explain: 주어는 가수·회사처럼 상품을 내놓는 쪽이에요. 앨범과 게임, 한정판처럼 가게에서 파는 물건에 어울리고, 앱은 '출시하다', 책은 '출간하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 팬이 앨범을 사는 건 '발매하다'가 아니라 '사다'예요.

phrases.en: That album was released yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품이 주어일 때 쓰는 피동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the product is the subject.

phrases.en: The company released the game as a limited edition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한정판처럼 가게에서 파는 물건과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with store-sold items such as limited editions.
phrases.en_equiv: to release as a limited edition

phrases.en: The company launched a new app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 서비스처럼 새로 내놓는 것에는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for newly launched things like apps or services.

explain_en: The subject is the one putting a product out, such as a singer or company. It suits albums, games and limited editions sold in stores; apps are 출시하다 and books 출간하다. A fan buying an album is simply 사다, not 발매하다.

examples.en: The graduation ceremony was held on a grand scale in the school auditorium.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 많은 손님 앞에서 결혼식을 성대히 올렸어요.
examples.en: The two held a grand wedding in front of many guests.
We plan to hold this year's festival in grand style too.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 팔순 잔치를 성대히 해 드렸어요.
examples.en: We threw a grand party for my grandfather's eightieth birthday.
The opening ceremony kicked off with great splendor.

examples.ko: 마을에서 새해맞이 행사를 성대히 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The village is preparing the New Year event on a grand scale.

explain: 결혼식, 잔치, 기념식, 개막식처럼 규모가 크고 화려한 행사 앞에 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '성대하게'나 '크게'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, '성대히'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: We held the birthday party grandly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성대히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 성대히, and sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: We held the shop's opening ceremony on a big scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 규모가 큰 행사를 쉽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, everyday way to say an event was large in scale.

phrases.en: A grand feast was held in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때는 '성대한' 꼴로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the 성대한 form when modifying a noun.

explain_en: It mostly goes with big, splendid events like weddings, parties and ceremonies. In daily talk people often say '성대하게' or '크게', while '성대히' appears more in news and writing.

examples.ko: 시청이 다음 달에 마라톤 대회를 주최해요.
examples.en: The city hall hosts a marathon next month.
Our school organized a speech contest.
Do you know who organized this event?

examples.ko: 회사에서 가족 초청 행사를 주최할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will host a family invitation event.

examples.ko: 행사를 주최하는 사람은 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: The person organizing an event has a lot to prepare.
I went to the festival organized by the city.

explain: 행사를 계획하고 여는 쪽을 '주최'라고 해요. 돈이나 물건으로 돕는 쪽은 '후원하다', 실제 운영을 맡는 쪽은 '주관하다'라서 서로 달라요. 집에서 파티를 열 때는 '열다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The company hosts a music festival in the fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사, 대회, 축제와 함께 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard pairing with events, contests, and festivals.

phrases.en: This contest is held, hosted by the city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 누가 여는지 밝힐 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in notices to say who is organizing the event.

phrases.en: The neighbors held a small market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '열다'가 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 열다 is easier and more natural in daily life.

explain_en: The side that plans and holds an event is the '주최'. The side that helps with money or goods is '후원하다' (sponsors), and the side that runs it in practice is '주관하다', so they differ. For a party at home, '열다' (to hold) is more natural.

dis.h: be the official organizer behind an event
gh: hold an event at a time or place
oversee and run an event or task

p.n: 개최하다 focuses on the event being held, not on who organizes it.

en: to draw lots; to cast lots

examples.en: We draw lots to pick who gets the prize.
We drew the winners yesterday.
I'll tell you right away once they draw the numbers.

examples.ko: 추첨하는 모습을 인터넷으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch the drawing online.
We drew lots for seats and then sat down.
We'll hold the drawing for the event gifts tomorrow.

explain: '뽑다'는 아무거나 고르는 일에도 쓰지만 추첨하다는 운에 맡겨 당첨자나 순서를 정할 때 써요. 뽑힌 사람은 '당첨되다'를 써요. 이벤트·기숙사·청약처럼 결과가 운으로 정해지는 곳에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: Dorm rooms are decided by lottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운에 맡겨 순서나 결과를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when order or results are decided by chance.

phrases.en: The store is holding a prize draw event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품을 추첨으로 주는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An event where prizes are given by drawing lots.

phrases.en: We draw lots and give gifts to three people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑은 사람에게 준다는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking phrase meaning to give to those drawn.

explain_en: '뽑다' (pick) can mean choosing anything, but 추첨하다 is for leaving it to luck to decide winners or order. The person who is chosen is '당첨되다'. You hear it for events, dorm rooms, and housing lotteries where luck decides.

examples.ko: 영화제 폐막 행사가 오늘 저녁에 열려요.
examples.en: The film festival's closing event is held this evening.

examples.ko: 폐막을 하루 앞두고 관객이 더 많아졌어요.
examples.en: With one day left before the closing, the crowds got even bigger.
Singers performed at the Olympic closing ceremony.
When is the closing date of this exhibition?

examples.ko: 박람회 폐막 후에도 홈페이지는 계속 열려 있어요.
examples.en: The website stays open even after the expo closes.
The festival announced its close with a splendid fireworks show.

explain: 영화제, 전시회, 올림픽, 박람회처럼 기간이 정해진 큰 행사가 끝날 때 써요. 반대말은 '개막'이고, '폐막식', '폐막작', '폐막일'처럼 뒤에 붙여 많이 말해요. 일반적인 일이 끝날 때는 '끝'이나 '끝나다'를 써요.

phrases.en: They announce the awards at the closing ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 끝내는 공식 의식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official ceremony that ends an event.

phrases.en: When is the closing day of the exhibition?
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 끝나는 날을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day an event ends.

phrases.example: 영화제 폐막 행사에 사람이 많이 왔어요.
phrases.en: Many people came to the film festival closing event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나는 날에 열리는 행사를 넓게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader term for events held on the closing day.

explain_en: It is used when a big event with a set period ends, such as a film festival, exhibition, Olympics or expo. The opposite is '개막', and it often combines as '폐막식', '폐막작' and '폐막일'. For ordinary things ending, use '끝' or '끝나다'.

en: party in honor of senior citizens

examples.en: A party for senior citizens was held at the village hall.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 경로잔치에서 노래 공연을 했어요.
examples.en: Our club performed songs at the senior citizens' party.

examples.ko: 경로잔치에 오신 어르신들께 도시락을 나눠 드렸어요.
examples.en: We handed out lunch boxes to the elders who came to the party.
The district office prepares a party for seniors every year.

examples.ko: 할머니는 경로잔치 날 곱게 한복을 입으셨어요.
examples.en: On the day of the senior party, my grandmother wore a beautiful hanbok.
Local shops sponsored the food for the senior citizens' party.

explain: '경로당, 경로석'처럼 어르신과 관련된 말에 '경로'가 나와요. 동네나 구청, 학교에서 여는 행사 이름으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The district office holds a senior citizens' party every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 준비하고 연다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for organizing and holding the event.

phrases.en: Grandmother attended the senior citizens' party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 손님으로 가는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the viewpoint of someone attending as a guest.

phrases.en: The school invited local seniors to the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신들을 모셔 오는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for inviting elders to the event.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to the senior party

explain_en: '경로' appears in other words about elders too, such as '경로당' and '경로석'. It is commonly used as the name of an event held by a neighborhood, district office or school.

examples.en: A return visit is scheduled for next month.
Expectations are high for the leader's return visit.
The schedule for the return visit hasn't been set yet.

examples.ko: 지난번 방문에 대한 답방으로 우리 집에 오셨어요.
examples.en: They came to our house as a return visit for our last visit.
When might a return visit be possible?

examples.ko: 두 나라는 답방 형식으로 교류를 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The two countries continued exchanges through reciprocal visits.

explain: 방문을 받았던 쪽이 답례로 상대를 다시 찾아가는 일이에요. 주로 외교나 정상회담 뉴스에서 나오고, 일상에서는 '놀러 가다', '찾아가다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The delegation will make a return visit next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 답방에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding '하다' to 답방.

phrases.en: The return visit will take place within this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 답방이 실제로 진행된다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the return visit actually happens; common in news.

phrases.en: The schedule for the return visit is not set yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방문 날짜나 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the dates or plan of the visit.

explain_en: It is when the side that received a visit goes to see the other side in return. It mostly appears in diplomacy and summit news, and in daily life people say things like '놀러 가다' or '찾아가다'.
